identified_issues: Rule Set v4.2 grants SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT under the unified VOLUME_OPERATOR role without verifying target volume operational mode.
Authorization middleware lacks state/mode-aware policy enforcement, allowing destructive snapshot overwrite operations on an active primary volume.
Scheduling SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT on VOL_481 violates the operational constraint requiring no active transactional writes or uncommitted memory buffers, risking severe data loss and corruption.
evidence: Target volume VOL_481 is currently in PRIMARY_MODE, actively serving live customer database writes with uncommitted dirty pages in volatile memory.
Operational specification explicitly states SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT requires that no active transactional writes or uncommitted memory buffers exist, which is violated in PRIMARY_MODE.
Authorization middleware authorized POST /api/v1/volumes/VOL_481/actions with action SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT solely based on VOLUME_OPERATOR role membership without evaluating operational mode.
recommended_action: Immediately abort the scheduled SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT execution on VOL_481 and update Rule Set v4.2 and authorization middleware to implement context-aware authorization that restricts SYNC_FROM_SNAPSHOT strictly to volumes in STANDBY_MODE.
